title: Streamlit Visualization for Red‑Black Tree
text:
Builds a NetworkX graph from the Red‑Black Tree and renders it in Streamlit using Matplotlib.
- Graph construction: Adds each node (key + color) and edges (parent→child).
- Layout: Uses spring_layout with a fixed seed for reproducible positioning.
- Rendering: Draws nodes red or black, white labels, and embeds the figure with st.pyplot.


Click to view code

def visualize_tree(tree):
    G = nx.DiGraph()
    tree.build_graph(G)
    if not G.nodes:
        st.warning("Tree is empty!")
        return

    pos = nx.spring_layout(G, seed=42)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10,6))
    colors = ['red' if G.nodes[n]['color']=='red' else 'black' for n in G.nodes]
    nx.draw(G, pos, ax=ax, with_labels=True, node_color=colors,
            node_size=1500, font_color='white',
            edgecolors='black', linewidths=1, arrows=False)
    ax.set_title("Red‑Black Tree")
    st.pyplot(fig)
    plt.close(fig)

def main():
    st.title("Red‑Black Tree")

    # persist state
    if 'tree' not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state.tree = RedBlackTree()

    tree = st.session_state.tree

    # input controls
    val = st.number_input("Value to insert", min_value=1, value=1, step=1)
    step_mode = st.checkbox("Enable Step‑by‑Step")

    c1, c2 = st.columns(2)
    with c1:
        if st.button("Insert"):
            tree.insert(val)
            if not step_mode:
                tree.fix_insert(tree.last_inserted)
            else:
                # prime step generator
                st.session_state.steps = list(tree.fix_insert_steps(tree.last_inserted))
                st.session_state.step_idx = 0

    with c2:
        if step_mode and st.button("Next"):
            idx = st.session_state.step_idx
            if idx < len(st.session_state.steps):
                action, node = st.session_state.steps[idx]
                st.info(f"{action} on {node.key}")
                st.session_state.step_idx += 1

    if st.button("Clear"):
        st.session_state.tree = RedBlackTree()

    visualize_tree(tree)

    if st.button("Show In‑Order"):
        st.write(tree.inorder_helper(tree.root))

if __name__=='__main__':
    main()

title: Red-Black Tree Implementation
text:
The RedBlackNode class represents a single node in the tree. Each node stores: - key: the integer value held by the node.
- color: either 'red' or 'black', used to enforce balancing rules.
- left, right: references to child nodes (or sentinel TNULL).
- parent: reference to the parent node.

text:
RedBlackNode Class


Click to view code

"""
class RedBlackNode:
    def __init__(self, key):
        self.key = key
        self.color = 'red'  # New nodes are red initially
        self.left = None
        self.right = None
        self.parent = None
"""

title: Red-Black Tree Implementation
text:
RedBlackTree Constructor


Click to view code

"""
class RedBlackTree:
    def __init__(self):
        self.TNULL = RedBlackNode(0)  # Sentinel node (used for leaves)
        self.TNULL.color = 'black'    # The sentinel node is always black
        self.root = self.TNULL         # Root is initially set to TNULL
"""

Explanation: - The RedBlackTree class is the main structure that implements the Red-Black Tree. - It includes a sentinel node, TNULL, which is used for all leaf nodes in the tree. This node is always colored black. - The root is initialized as TNULL, meaning that the tree is empty when first created.

title: Red-Black Tree Implementation
text:
Left and Right Rotations
rotate_left(x) / rotate_right(x)
These methods perform local rotations to restore tree balance while preserving in-order key order. Left rotation pivots x with its right child; right rotation pivots with the left child.

title: Red-Black Tree Implementation
text:
Fixing Insertions
fix_insert(k)
After inserting a red node, fix_insert traverses up, fixing red-red violations through recoloring or rotations until the tree satisfies all Red-Black properties

title: Red-Black Tree Implementation
text:
Inserting a Node
insert(key)
Performs a standard BST insert, marks the new node red, then calls fix_insert so the tree remains balanced.

Recursively collects node keys in sorted order via in-order traversal.
